criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`. A new fixture test has two runs for the same SHA, a `pull_request` run with the newer created_at and a different conclusion, and a `push` run on `athena/ci/<job id>`. It shows that only the push run's result is returned.
criteria.evidence: I ran it: `ci_push_run_wins_over_newer_pull_request_run ... ok` (95 passed, 0 failed). The test sets up a pull_request run (id 20, created 00:30, failure) and a push run on CI_BRANCH (id 10, created 00:10, success). It checks that both `parse_ci_run` and `ci_source(CI_BRANCH).fetch` return address ci/10 with conclusion success, and that the jobs call is for runs/10. It also checks the reverse case: a newer green pull_request run does not hide a red push run. The old code picked the newest `ci` run of any event, so it would return run 20 and these assertions would fail.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`. A new test where only a `pull_request` run exists, or a push run exists on another branch, shows that the source returns no result (None), so `resolve` reports it missing and never uses that run.
criteria.evidence: `ci_push_run_ignores_other_events_and_branches ... ok`. It covers three cases: a pull_request run on CI_BRANCH, a push run on athena/ci/another-job, and a push run on main. In each case the canned reply ignores the query and holds a green run for the right SHA. Even so, `parse_ci_run` returns None, `fetch` returns Ok(None), and no jobs call is made. `resolve` then returns Failed with Source::Local, and the failing local fake is called exactly once.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`. A new test shows that the HTTP path built by the CI source includes `event=push` and the branch name. Use the recording transport in gh/tests.rs if present, or assert on the built query.
criteria.evidence: `ci_push_run_query_names_event_and_branch ... ok`. The recording CiRunner captures the paths of the `gh api` calls. The first path starts with `repos/example/project/actions/runs?` and contains `head_sha=<sha>`, `event=push` and `branch=athena/ci/20261031-142738-g437`. The second path is exactly `actions/runs/10/jobs?filter=latest&per_page=100`. In client.rs (line 724) the query is built as `actions/runs?head_sha={sha}&event={CI_EVENT}&branch={branch}&per_page=20`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core gh`. A new fixture test shows that a failed aggregate `fmt, clippy, tests` job gives red steps, and a successful one gives green steps for all three check names. The current behaviour of copying the `cargo fmt --check` step to all three checks is gone (Grep for `CI_CHECK_STEP` in client.rs).
criteria.evidence: `ci_push_run_verdict_comes_from_the_aggregate_job ... ok`. A failed aggregate with a failed clippy job gives conclusion failure, with clippy failure and fmt/test success. A failed fmt job gives the same pattern for fmt, and a failed test shard makes the test step red. A successful aggregate gives three success steps named fmt, clippy and test, including when the check jobs were skipped. The test also covers cancelled, gate-failure, in-progress, history-only-failure and missing-aggregate cases. A Grep for `CI_CHECK_STEP` in crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs finds nothing. The job names in the code match ci.yml, which I read: `fmt` (line 109), `clippy` (188), `test (shard ${{ matrix.shard }})` (269) and `fmt, clippy, tests` (401).

criteria.criterion: crates/athena-core/src/gh/client.rs filters runs on `event` and `head_branch`. The other changed files are crates/athena-core/src/gh/tests.rs and, only if needed, ci_result.rs call sites. No change appears in run/mod.rs, ci.yml, athena.toml or CHANGELOG.md.

findings.summary: The brief contradicts itself on CHANGELOG.md. The expected deliverables list it, but criterion 5 and follow-up C keep it out of this slice. The candidate follows criterion 5 and leaves it unchanged.
findings.evidence: The expected deliverables list `CHANGELOG.md (modify)`. Criterion 5 says 'No change appears in ... CHANGELOG.md', and the out-of-scope section says follow-up C adds the CHANGELOG.md entry. `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` shows CHANGELOG.md unchanged.

findings.summary: `aggregate_verdict` hard-codes the ci.yml job names `fmt`, `clippy` and the `test (` prefix. If a job is renamed in ci.yml, a red push run would silently read as `unusable`, and Athena would fall back to the local checks.
findings.evidence: In client.rs, the `behind` closure matches `n.starts_with("test (")` or `n == other`. These names match ci.yml lines 109, 188 and 269 today. Nothing ties them to the workflow file, so a rename would break the match without any error. The failure mode is safe: Athena falls back to the local checks and never uses a wrong green. A later change could add a test that reads the job names from ci.yml.

summary: The change does what the accepted reading asks, and I recommend it pass. The GitHub CI result fetch now trusts only the newest `push` run of the `ci` workflow on `athena/ci/<job id>`. A new `GhClient::ci_source(branch)` returns a `CiBranchSource` that implements `CiSource`, so the trait signature is unchanged. The runs query adds `event=push&branch=<branch>`, and `pick_ci_run` filters on `event` and `head_branch` again as a second guard. The verdict now comes from the aggregate `fmt, clippy, tests` job. The old copying of the `cargo fmt --check` step result to all three checks is gone: `CI_CHECK_STEP` no longer appears in client.rs. I ran `cargo test -p athena-core gh` and all 95 tests passed, including the four new ones. Together they show: the push run wins over a newer pull_request run in both directions; a pull_request run or a push run on another branch gives None, and `resolve` then falls back to the local checks; the built query names the event and the branch; and red and green verdicts come from the aggregate job. Each test would fail against the old selection or parsing code. Only gh/client.rs and gh/tests.rs changed. Athena's recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. There are two small notes. The brief contradicts itself on CHANGELOG.md, and the candidate follows criterion 5 by leaving it unchanged. The job names from ci.yml are hard-coded in the code; a future rename would cause a fallback to the local checks rather than a wrong result.
